correctness.rationale: For every positive J1,J2,kappa, spectral dissipation and connectivity force all eigenvalues of Q into the left half-plane; the finite-time survival integral is the uniquely determined Hermitian solution to \(Q^\dagger X+XQ=-I\). All nine matrix entries of the displayed X satisfy the identity symbolically, and its 3,3 entry is the claimed first-absorption mean. AM–GM in the exact coupling ratio x and factorization (x-2)^2(2x+1)/(2x^2) establish global lower bound 3/sqrt(E) with equality iff x=2,kappa=2sqrt(E). Independently solved sample Lyapunov systems match. There are no endpoint minimizers because the sharp ratio bound diverges at x downarrow0 and x to infinity.

value.rationale: Three sites are the smallest linear transfer network with two independently designable hopping links. A fixed sum of squared link strengths has concrete operator-norm/engineering meaning, and the one-shot mean absorption time is a natural performance metric exhibiting a nontrivial competition between Zeno suppression and slow trapping. The theorem completely classifies the exact joint global optimum, forces an asymmetric 2:1 squared resource split rather than the usual homogeneous assumption, and establishes a 13.4% transport-time gain against the best equal-link design. No paper-sized generalization is needed for this natural complete constrained-design problem. Strict scope to the specified cost and finite geometry is important.
